name: [WEEKLY] SSRF-Driven Secret Egress: Public-Facing App Reaches Cloud Metadata/Attacker Host
description: Detects an unauthenticated public-facing application that, shortly after receiving an inbound request, makes a server-side outbound connection to the cloud instance-metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254 / fd00:ec2::254) or an attacker-named callback host — the tell-tale of a server-side request forgery being used to steal secrets. This matters this fortnight because a cluster of maximum-severity advisories all share this exact primitive: OpenDJ's DSMLv2 gateway dereferences attacker-supplied xsd:anyURI values (GHSA-68r5-9hpg-7qw9), Flyto2 Core's unauthenticated /run reflects callback_url and attaches X-Internal-Key: $FLYTO_RUNNER_SECRET (CVE-2026-67426), and Budibase forwards stored REST-datasource credentials to any host a query names (GHSA-mqhr-6j6h-74p5) — with OpenAM (CVE-2026-62379) and Ruflo MCP (CVE-2026-59726) providing the unauthenticated RCE that reaches the same egress. It spans the exploit (T1190) → credential-access (IMDS/secret read) → exfiltration (secret leaves over the app's own socket) kill-chain stages. It FIRES when a server runtime (java, node, ruby, python, w3wp, nginx) egresses to a metadata IP or listed C2 host within the correlation window of an inbound public request, and when EC2 instance-role credentials appear off-instance; it does NOT fire on normal user browsing, on SDK-driven IMDS calls that never follow an inbound public request, or on internal-only service-to-service traffic.
query: Image:(*169.254.169.254* OR *java.exe* OR *javaw.exe* OR *node.exe* OR *ruby.exe* OR *python.exe* OR *python3* OR *php\-fpm* OR *w3wp.exe* OR *nginx.exe* OR *httpd* OR *InboundConnectionAccepted* OR *Public* OR *ConnectionSuccess*)
